title: Closed support for abelian pro-etale sheaves
statement: Use [def-weil-size-convention] and the pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let i:Z→X be a closed immersion of schemes and j:U→X its quasi-compact open complement. For inverse image i* and direct image i_* on sheaves of abelian groups, as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], the counit i*i_*→id is an isomorphism. For every abelian sheaf F on X with j*F zero, the actual unit F→i_*i*F is an isomorphism. There is no qcqs assumption on X and no restriction on the coefficient abelian sheaves.

source.place: Tags 09AA (closed immersion counit) and 09AH (short exact sequence for a quasi-compact complementary open); Modules on Sites, integral coefficient action.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-abelian-closed-counit] for the closed counit. Independently prove the supported-unit assertion by joint conservativity of the two restrictions, as follows.

Suppose a section maps to zero under inverse image for a scheme map g. Inverse image is sheafification of a left Kan extension. Local injectivity of sheafification gives a pro-etale cover on which that equality holds in the Kan extension. The relevant comma category is filtered, and the underlying-set functor of abelian groups preserves its colimit, so the equality holds at a stage: locally the section vanishes after restriction along an object over X whose base change receives that member of the cover. This is the explicit private lemma abLocalVanish; it adapts the proved source module UpperLowerStar.Detection to abelian groups and the current finite-coefficient API.

For a finite quasi-compact jointly surjective family g_k, choose those covers for every k. The source theorem QuasiCompactCover.of_comp_factor says their weakly-etale neighborhoods together are a quasi-compact covering family over the original object. Joint surjectivity follows by lifting a point to a fibre product and then to a covering member. Each neighborhood is weakly etale over the base by cancellation from its structural map. Thus this is a pro-etale cover. The original section vanishes by the separated sheaf condition. Apply this to each section in the image of a sheaf morphism and use naturality of the inverse-image unit to prove joint faithfulness.

Take the two-element family formed by i and j. Closed immersions are quasi-compact, and the ranges cover X by the complement hypothesis. If both restrictions of F are zero, both restrictions of its identity morphism vanish; joint faithfulness implies that identity is zero. Since inverse images are exact, apply this zero detection to the kernel and cokernel of a morphism to obtain joint detection of isomorphisms. These are the proved private lemmas abJointZero and abDetectIso.

For the unit F→i_*i*F, its closed restriction is invertible because its composite with the invertible closed counit is the identity by the adjunction triangle identity. If j*F is zero, its open restriction has zero source and target: the target j*i_*i*F has sections of i*F on empty base changes, hence is zero. The sheaf condition for the empty cover supplies the terminal, thus zero, sections. Joint detection of isomorphisms now proves the actual closed unit invertible. No ringed-module comparison or localization sequence is assumed.

proof_origin.place: Closed counit from Tags 09AA/09BL; supported units proved directly by local injectivity of sheafification, filtered Kan-extension stages, quasi-compact covering factorization and joint restriction conservativity. Formal adaptation of the proved source Detection and ClosedImmersion arguments to Ab.

lean.statement:
theorem abelian_closed_support {X U Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (j : U ⟶ X)
    [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (hij : Set.range j = (Set.range i)ᶜ) :
    IsIso (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction Ab.{u + 1} i).counit ∧
    ∀ F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1},
      IsZero ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} j).obj F) →
      IsIso ((upperStarLowerStarAdjunction Ab.{u + 1} i).unit.app F)
